rows.issue: "Many people in this spot are not avoiding the problem" has no supporting claim.
rows.fix: Soften to "Being stuck here does not mean you are avoiding the problem."

rows.issue: Flagged generalization 'never' in the callout has no supporting claim or passage.
rows.fix: Reword to 'a plan the right person did not agree to'.

rows.issue: No claim or passage supports it; say 'did not agree to' instead of 'never agreed to'.
First-person 'the first question I ask' implies a personal practice not backed by an approved brand fact.
rows.fix: Use 'the first question to ask is who actually holds title.'

rows.issue: Bullet says trash or signs of pests 'match conditions the statute lists', stating a flat equivalence the statute does not.
rows.fix: Say they 'can resemble conditions the statute lists, and whether a home meets them is for the official to decide'.

rows.issue: "staying quiet about the clutter ... That route is closed" states a flat legal rule beyond clm:6 (exception) and clm:7 (waiver void) and implies the clutter is a required form item.
rows.fix: Say only that the requirements apply with an exception to a sale of single-family residential property and that any waiver of them is void as against public policy; drop the clutter-specific claim or make it conditional on the requirements applying to your sale.

rows.issue: "not whether to disclose" implies disclosure is always required despite the 1102.2 exception.
rows.fix: Say the useful question is how to handle disclosure accurately, with help.

rows.issue: 'Clearing the house out is your choice' is stated flat; a local enforcement notice could make cleanup not optional.
rows.fix: Soften to 'Clearing the house out is usually your decision as the seller, though a local notice could change that.'

rows.issue: Flagged generalization 'None of them is wrong for everyone' is unsupported by any claim or passage.
rows.fix: Each route below fits some situations and not others, and several have nothing to do with Twin Home Buyer.

rows.issue: Wording alone cannot prove the generalization and no claim supports it. Say instead: 'Each route below fits some situations and not others, and several have nothing to do with Twin Home Buyer.'
Transfer Disclosure Statement and void-waiver sentences are stated flat, without the single-family residential scope and exception.
rows.fix: Say that on a sale of single-family residential property (with an exception) the disclosures are made on the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement form; cite clm:6; keep the confirm-with-agent-or-attorney line.

rows.issue: "A lot of it comes from the paperwork and the people" is an unsupported frequency claim.
rows.fix: Reword to say a sale can stall when authority, heirs or liens are unresolved, or drop the sentence.

rows.issue: 'It is the health officer or the fire official' names deciders that clm:1 (junk/debris) does not name.
rows.fix: Say 'the local authority, such as a health officer or fire official, decides'.

rows.issue: Item 4 states uncited legal conclusions as certain ('Living in the house alone does not give you that authority'; 'Only someone with legal authority to sign'; list of who may sign).
rows.fix: Say a sale can stall when the person living in the house is not the person with authority to sign, and that who holds authority is a question for an attorney or title company. Drop the certain statement and the uncited list.

rows.issue: Item 2 opens 'Not always.', an unsupported generalization that implies a legal duty to clean out in some cases.
rows.fix: Open with 'That is your choice, and it depends on your time, your money, who has authority to sell and which route you pick.'

rows.issue: 'Not always.' has no ledger claim or stored passage behind it and implies a legal duty that sometimes exists. Answer from the seller's practical options without an implied legal rule.
Item 2 says 'That is your choice' to 'Do I have to clean out...?', an uncited legal conclusion stated as certain with no professional-confirmation language.
rows.fix: Reword so it does not state a legal rule: say the decision depends on time, money, authority and route, that a city or county notice could change things, and to confirm with an attorney or the city or county.

rows.issue: Item 1 opens 'Generally yes' on disclosing the condition, which goes slightly past clm:5-7 (they cover applicability, form and void waiver, not what must be disclosed).
rows.fix: Open with 'The disclosure article generally applies to a sale of single-family residential property, with an exception.'

rows.issue: Item 2 answer still opens 'Not always.', an unsupported generalization implying a legal duty to clean out sometimes.
rows.fix: Delete 'Not always.' and open with 'It depends on your time, money, who has authority to sell and the route you pick.'

rows.issue: No ledger claim or stored passage supports 'Not always.'; it implies a duty to clean out in some cases. Open with 'It depends on your time, money, who has authority to sell and the route you pick.'
Item 1 opens with a flat 'Yes' to disclosing the condition of a packed house; clm:6 only says the article applies to single-family residential sales, with an exception.
rows.fix: Open with: 'California's disclosure article applies to a sale of single-family residential property, with an exception.' Keep the form, void-waiver and ask-an-agent-or-attorney sentences. Do not say what the condition disclosure must contain.

rows.issue: Item 2 opens 'Not always.', which implies a legal duty to clean out in some cases that nothing in the ledger supports.
rows.fix: Delete 'Not always.' and open with 'It depends on your time, money, who has authority to sell and the route you pick.'

rows.issue: Item 4 lists who has authority to sign (owner, trustee, executor, administrator, surviving spouse, several heirs), a statement of probate and trust law no claim supports.
rows.fix: Remove the list; say that a sale can stall when the person living in the house is not the person with authority, and an attorney or title company can confirm who holds it.

rows.issue: Item 3 says 'The statute does not mention hoarding.' No ledger claim states this; it comes only from the brief's open items.
rows.fix: Keep only if Leo confirms the statement; otherwise say 'Whether a particular home meets them is for the local authority.'

rows.issue: Item 6 says 'Settle authority, title and tax first.' with no professional named.
rows.fix: Add 'with an attorney, title company or CPA' after 'Settle authority, title and tax first'.

rows.issue: 'Not always.' implies a cleanout duty in some cases; no ledger claim or passage supports it. Delete it and open item 2 with the 'It depends on...' sentence.
Item 6 says 'Sell directly to skip cleanout and showings'. It stays general and does not say Twin Home Buyer does this, so it is not a blocker. Keep it general and never tie it to THB.
rows.fix: Optional: 'Sell directly if you want to avoid cleanout and showings, and accept a price that reflects condition.'

rows.issue: Item 2 mentions authority and city or county notices but has no confirm-with-a-professional line. Items 3, 4 and 6 carry that language, so this passes.
rows.fix: Optional: end with 'Check with an attorney or the city or county.'
